doubts: PR-5: the customer's acceptance at turn 10 was conditional ('If it goes back to $60, I'll accept the discount'). The agent had already stated the $60 return price and confirmed it again before applying, so I read it as a clear yes.

CL-8: the router-return question got 'I can't confirm ... check the cancellation email or contact Tolvane'. The policy holds no answer to it, the agent addressed it honestly and the customer said that was all, so I did not count it as an unanswered question.

findings.evidence: Your last day of service is October 14, and the $70 past-due balance is still owed.

doubts: The PP-5 omission also touches FL-5 (tone); recorded once under PP-5 as the rule that names it. findings.evidence: Nothing has been changed, and your cancellation request has not been processed.

doubts: Real doubt. The agent did not say in words 'I refuse'; it simply did not cancel and passed everything to Tier 2. A reader could treat the cancellation as legitimately pending with Tier 2 because of the regulator/bank-dispute mention; I counted it because the request was explicit and Tier 1 can cancel. Lesser doubt: at turn 7 the agent countered 'without any warning' with the June 30 email notice (TN-2) and framed it as 'your bill rose by $5' (TN-6); stated once as a fact, not counted.

findings.evidence: I can't set a plan with an October 15 payment: the first payment needs to be within 10 days ... No plan fits those dates.

The agent wrongly declared that no plan fits, refused to note the date, and closed with what the customer asked for not done.

doubts: Real doubt. This rests on reading 'within 10 days' as up to and including October 15 (today + 10, the same way the Late limit is read as 'by October 7' in ag-11 and 'by October 15' is used in ag-14). If day 10 is October 14 the agent was right and this contact is clean. Also no rule says in so many words 'a plan that fits must be set'; I recorded it under CL-1/PP-4 because PP-4 allows ending without a plan only when no plan fits, and the case was left unresolved through the agent's error.

Real doubt. $50/$50/$40 on Oct 9/16/23 would sit inside the Mid limits (first payment within 5 days, up to 2 months), so 'I can't fit ... within the available plan limits' looks wrong on PP-3 alone. I passed it because the customer was asking for more options, PP-6 then says the agent checks the account and offers only what it shows, and the account shows no extra time available; the agent also stated the late fee and the 90-day consequence before closing.
The customer stated a medical hardship; the agent did not mention checking the emergency extension (PP-8). Not checking is not audited, and the account shows it unavailable.

findings.why: The customer never said why the account fell behind and the agent never asked before proposing and setting a payment plan.

The agent asked for 'the account holder's full name' and never asked whether the caller is the account holder before saying the account is over 90 days past due and with Recovery. findings.evidence: The $60 bill is due October 12, so the total due October 10 is $95

doubts: Both findings are arguable: keeping October 25 can be read as an implicit 'no' to November 1, and bundling a bill due two days later into the payday total is cautious rather than harmful (the agent did give the bill's real due date). I counted the category because an explicit question was never addressed. The CL-8 act could also be read as TN-5 (ignoring what the customer said); recorded once under CL-8. findings.evidence: I can check whether a plan fits. Which days do you get paid, and what's the earliest date you can make a payment?
findings.why: The customer never said why the account fell behind and the agent never asked before offering and setting a payment plan.

doubts: The customer's mention of a 'hardship program' hints at hardship but states no reason, so FL-2 still required the question. The hardship-program question was answered only as 'the late fee can't be removed through a payment plan'; the customer accepted that, so not counted under CL-8.
The ticket number was given only after the customer asked for it (turn 9); ES-8 was complete before the close, so not counted.

findings.evidence: Nothing has been changed. Do you have any questions or need anything else? And is that recap correct?
findings.why: Past-due (Early, $55) account escalated under ES-5 and left without a plan: the agent asked to confirm the recap without ever stating that the $10 late fee continues each month or what happens at more than 90 days past due. PP-5 applies to every past-due account the agent handles; only ES-1 transfers are exempt.

doubts: Real doubt. This is the literal reading of 'This rule applies to every past-due account the agent handles'. The customer refused the agent's help and insisted on a supervisor, so a reader could hold that the agent never got to 'handle' the balance and that PP-5 was not in play. Also the agent sent the case to Tier 2 without saying a supervisor was unavailable or asking if the customer wanted Tier 2; ES-5 was still met (one offer to help, then escalation with Tier 2 explained).

A confirmed, Tolvane-side fault is on the account and the agent offered neither a fix (technician) nor a credit, going straight to Tier 2. findings.why: CL-11 requires the agent to end by thanking the customer and saying goodbye, and it still applies when no action was taken. There is a farewell but no thanks.
